question: A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a motorcycle accident 30 minutes ago. He was found at the scene of the accident with a major injury to the anterior chest by a metallic object that was not removed during transport to the hospital. The medical history could not be obtained. His blood pressure is 80/50 mm Hg, pulse is 130/min, and respiratory rate is 40/min. Evaluation upon arrival to the emergency department reveals a sharp metal object penetrating through the anterior chest to the right of the sternum at the 4th intercostal space. The patient is taken to the operating room immediately, where it is shown the heart has sustained a major injury. Which of the following arteries supplies the part of the heart most likely injured in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Metallic object injury to the anterior chest" -> "Penetrated through the 4th intercostal space to the right of the sternum" -> "Heart sustained a major injury" -> "Likely injury to the right coronary artery" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Major injury to the heart" -> "Right coronary artery most likely affected" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Metallic object injury to the anterior chest" -> "Heart injury confirmed in the operating room" -> "Injury likely involves the right coronary artery" -> 75%
enhanced_information: The likely artery injured in this patient, based on the location of the penetrating object and confirmed heart injury, is the right coronary artery.
analysis: The core medical principle in this scenario involves understanding the coronary artery anatomy and its relation to the heart's blood supply. The right coronary artery is the most likely artery injured in this patient based on the location of the penetrating object to the right of the sternum at the 4th intercostal space and the confirmed heart injury. The right coronary artery supplies the right atrium, right ventricle, and the inferior part of the left ventricle, making it the artery most likely affected in this case.
